summary: Mid-stream silence followed by timeout during prolonged token emission for high-output requests
description: Issue summary: Customer reports repeated mid-stream silence during streaming generation for requests with very large max_tokens and a high client-side burst rate. After a prolonged quiet period (typically 18-30s, sometimes longer) the client receives an HTTP 504 / connection reset. Impact: Blocks CuraLogix nightly batch report generation job; multiple requests failing intermittently and causing downstream ETL retries and invoice-impacting SLA violations. Environment: Dedicated capacity in prod-us-east using redwood-rlhf-13b-v2; model pinned by customer to v2; traffic pattern is short bursts of 6 parallel very-large-output requests during batch windows (max_tokens between 75k-150k). Observed behavior: partial token stream arrives (~20-30% of expected tokens), then a silence gap, then connection resets/504 after ~90s. Expected behavior: steady streaming until finalization and clean 200 with stream close. Severity/Scope: reproducible in customer's nightly job; affects ~40% of batch runs in last 48 hours.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use dedicated tenant in prod-us-east with model redwood-rlhf-13b-v2 pinned
2) Send 6 parallel streaming generate requests with max_tokens ~100000 and prefix length ~2k tokens
3) Observe token emission for first ~10-30s, then silence for 20-30s, then client error (HTTP 504 or ECONNRESET) around 90s total wall time
4) Repeat during peak batch window to reproduce consistently
logs: Customer client log: "stream chunk received (partial), then socket write EPIPE at 2026-03-09T23:14:22Z"
Gateway tail: 2026-03-09T23:14:20Z GET /v1/generate STREAM id=tx-9a3c status=200 chunks=12 then no data for 24s then upstream reset (504)
Serving-runtime: trace tx-9a3c kernel-swap triggered at 23:14:21Z queue-depth=18 mem-pressure=0.78 eviction=delayed
Scheduler logs: priority inversion observed, long-running large-token job preempted synchronous finalizer on same GPU at 23:14:19Z
comments: 2026-03-10 08:12 Priya Nair (Support): Customer first reported: batch job failing intermittently with mid-stream silence then timeout. Attached client logs. Asked for request IDs and timestamps.

2026-03-10 09:03 Marco Alvarez (SRE): Pulled traces for tenant cura-123. Observed repeated kernel-swap and queue spikes coincident with customer batch windows. Opening investigation into batching and KV cache eviction behavior.

2026-03-10 11:20 CuraLogix (Customer): We can reproduce reliably when running 6 concurrent huge-output requests. Reducing to 2 concurrent requests appears to avoid the silence. We need a workaround while you investigate.

2026-03-11 02:05 Marco Alvarez (SRE): Hypothesis: combination of large max_tokens + client burst causes prolonged GPU kernel swapping and preemption of finalizer threads -> streaming heartbeat gaps. Also saw HTTP/2 WINDOW_UPDATE stalling on the streaming proxy during the silence windows.

2026-03-12 16:40 Priya Nair (Support): Proposed temporary mitigations to customer (listed below). Waiting on customer confirmation of mitigation tests. Assigned follow-up to runtime team to add telemetry for long-tail emission gaps.
investigation_notes: Telemetry: added fine-grained emit-heartbeat spans to serving-runtime to capture silence windows; initial traces show emit heartbeat not fired for 18-28s in impacted traces
Hypothesis A: adaptive batching policy attempted to coalesce large-token requests leading to head-of-queue blocking and priority inversion for finalizer tasks
Hypothesis B: KV cache compaction/eviction path paused token emission while serializing very large KV pages to disk in rare cases
Hypothesis C: streaming-proxy HTTP/2 window management stalled when a single connection carried large unacknowledged frames (need to correlate with proxy-level window metrics)
Repro test: Reduced parallelism to 2/6 in dedicated tenant replicated issue disappearance; suggests contention rather than model correctness
Trace pointers: tx-9a3c, tx-9a7f, tx-9b01 show similar silence signatures around kernel-swap events

Next steps: (1) coordinate with runtime team to add backpressure limits for extremely large max_tokens per tenant; (2) add proxy-level per-stream WINDOW_UPDATE timeouts and more aggressive keepalive; (3) consider server-side enforced soft cap on concurrent very-large-output streaming slots per GPU
resolution: Mitigations proposed and partial workarounds provided to customer. Temporary workarounds: limit concurrent very-large-output streams to <=2 during batch window, lower max_tokens to <=50k where possible, and enable small-stream-chunking (client-side) so proxy-level WINDOW_UPDATE is exercised more frequently. Runtime/infra actions: runtime team to add telemetry and a patch to avoid long finalizer preemption; proxy team to harden HTTP/2 window handling. Target follow-up for patch rollouts scheduled: runtime patch PR and proxy config change. Status: awaiting customer validation of temporary mitigations and runtime team ETA for patch.
